# FDG7007

> DO NOT have public members that can either throw or not throw based on some option.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.1 Exception Throwing.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG7007
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Do not let the parameter '{0}' decide whether '{1}' throws

Library only: the text scopes it to public members, whose callers outside the library would have to make the decision (the Abrams annotation). FDG7007 reports a bool parameter whose first word is "throw" (throwOnError, throwIfNotFound), as in the body's GetType example, on an externally visible method, constructor or indexer. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, since their parameters come from the member they override or implement. Options of other types (an enum or a settings object) are not seen, so coverage is partial. Removing the parameter changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
// bad design
public Type GetType(string name, bool throwOnError)
```

> **Brad Abrams:** An API such as this one usually reflects the inability of the framework designer to make a decision. A method either completes successfully or it does not, in which case it should throw an exception. Failure to decide forces the decision on the caller of the API, which likely does not have enough context on implementation details of the API to make an informed decision.
